description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Steely is hiring an entry-level Software Engineer focused on network software. The role involves developing software and applying networking and network-security concepts in a mission-focused technical environment.
Entry-Level Software Engineer specializing in software engineering with a network focus

Requirements:
• Candidates must be able to hold and maintain a security clearance, therefore U.S. citizenship is required
• Experience developing software in Rust
• Experience developing software on Linux
• Experience with Docker or containerized applications
• Experience with GitLab, GitHub, or similar software development platforms
• Experience with CI/CD or automated build and test pipelines
• Experience with automated unit or integration testing
• Experience with networking or network-security software through coursework, projects, internships, research, or other relevant experience
• Experience developing REST APIs, backend services, or web applications
• Familiarity with TCP/IP, UDP, TLS, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, routing, NAT, and VPN technologies
• Familiarity with cryptography, including encryption, hashing, public/private keys, certificates, and PKI
• Familiarity with Linux networking tools such as ip, ss, ping, tcpdump, and Wireshark
• Familiarity with authentication and authorization, including OIDC or OAuth 2.0
• Familiarity with multithreaded, concurrent, or asynchronous programming
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
• Demonstrated understanding of software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, testing, debugging, error handling, and maintainable software design
• Experience developing software in Rust, Java, C++, or another strongly typed programming language, through coursework, internships, research, personal projects, or other relevant experience
• Familiarity with Linux and command-line tools
• Familiarity with Git and source-control concepts
• Understanding of fundamental computer networking concepts, including IP addressing, TCP, UDP, and client/server communication
• Experience developing software collaboratively, including working with others on code and incorporating code review feedback
• Demonstrated ability to learn new programming languages, technologies, and development tools
• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
• Effective written and verbal communication skills
• Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance; therefore, U.S. citizenship is required
